did: Built KPLAY's first two stories, the parts the Korean drama replacement stands on. KP1 is a catalogue of twenty Korean endings that join two clauses (because, if, when, but, so that), each with what it does and what it won't allow, written so code can check a scene's focus or a spoken reach. KP2 conjugates both ways over that catalogue and a fifty-nine-word list: a word plus an ending gives the right form, a form gives every reading that rebuilds it, and a near miss like 왔어서, 이워서 or 춥어요 is refused with the rule it breaks. The stem changes come from an open-source conjugator, pinned; the rest is ours. Read aloud and the grammar lens are untouched.

calls.title: The catalogue lands before its rules are cited (C1085)
options: land it with every grade marked unchecked and the rules from standard teaching grammar
hold it until a session can read the curriculum list and the learners' dictionary
calls.why: The two Korean government sites that state these rules refused this session's connections; the catalogue says plainly that every grade is unchecked, reviewers checked the grammar twice, and #2850 stays open for the citing step.
calls.undo: Hold KPLAY's later stories until a session cites a source for each rule and corrects any it gets wrong.

calls.title: Conjugation uses an open-source library (C1086)
options: use @dongsa/conjugation for the stem changes and build only our part
calls.why: It already handles every irregular class, is MIT licensed, makes no network calls, and a test holds it to agree with our own word list; the coordinator admitted it before it was added.
calls.undo: Remove the package and write the stem changes in the conjugation module, keeping its tests.
